learn.hook: From snowy peaks to sandy deserts and sunny beaches, India packs almost every kind of land into one country. How?
points: India is a land of great geographical diversity: mountains, plains, plateaus, deserts, coasts and islands.

Geographers group India's land into physical regions: the Himalayas in the north, the Northern Plains, the Thar Desert in the west, the Peninsular Plateau in the south, the coastal plains, and the islands.
Each region has its own landforms, rivers, soils, plants and animals, so people's food, homes, clothes and work also differ from region to region.
The Aravalli hills in Rajasthan are among the oldest fold mountains in the world; they are now worn down and much lower than the Himalayas.
This variety of land is one big reason for India's variety of cultures.

example.q: Why does a farmer in Punjab grow wheat on flat fields, while a family in Ladakh herds yaks and goats?
steps: Punjab lies in the Northern Plains, with flat land, fertile soil brought by rivers and plenty of water.
Ladakh lies in the high, cold, dry mountains where farming is difficult and the season is short.
Animals like yaks and goats can survive the cold and give milk, wool and transport.
example.answer: Because the physical region (flat fertile plains versus cold high mountains) shapes how people earn their living.

learn.reallife: When you travel by train from Delhi to Chennai, you watch flat plains change to rocky plateau land outside your window.

games.title: True or false: regions of India
items: The Thar Desert lies mainly in Rajasthan.
Most of the Thar Desert is in western Rajasthan.
The Northern Plains are made of soil carried down by rivers.
The Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra and their tributaries laid down this soil, called alluvium.
The Aravallis are younger than the Himalayas.
The Aravallis are much older; they are among the oldest fold mountains on Earth.
India has island groups in both the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal.
Lakshadweep is in the Arabian Sea; the Andaman and Nicobar Islands are in the Bay of Bengal.
All of India gets the same kind of land and weather.
India has mountains, plains, deserts, plateaus and coasts, each with different conditions.

quiz.q: Which physical region of India lies to the far north?
quiz.explain: The Himalayan mountains form India's northern boundary like a great wall.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the positions of India's regions on the map

quiz.q: The Thar Desert is found mainly in which state?
quiz.explain: The Thar, or Great Indian Desert, covers much of western Rajasthan.
quiz.mistake: Does not link the desert to the dry north-west of India

quiz.q: Which hills in Rajasthan are among the oldest fold mountains in the world?
quiz.explain: The Aravallis are extremely old and have been worn down over a very long time.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the tallest mountains must be the oldest

quiz.q: Why are the Northern Plains so good for farming?
options: They are made of hard rock
Rivers have spread fertile soil over flat land
quiz.explain: Rivers from the Himalayas deposit fine fertile soil (alluvium), and the land is flat with plenty of water.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect rivers with fertile soil

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT one of India's physical regions?
quiz.explain: The Sahara is in Africa. India's desert is the Thar.
quiz.mistake: Confuses world deserts with India's Thar Desert

quiz.q: How does India's variety of landforms affect people's lives?
options: It has no effect at all
It shapes their food, homes, clothes and work
It only changes the colour of the soil
It makes everyone grow the same crop
quiz.explain: People adapt to their land: flat plains suit farming, mountains suit herding, coasts suit fishing.
quiz.mistake: Thinks geography and daily life are unconnected

quiz.q: A region of high flat land, raised above the land around it, is called a:
quiz.explain: A plateau is a raised, fairly flat area, like a table-top. The Deccan Plateau is an example.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up a plateau (raised) with a plain (low and flat)

quiz.q: Which island group of India lies in the Arabian Sea?
quiz.explain: Lakshadweep lies off the coast of Kerala in the Arabian Sea.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the two island groups and their seas

teach.ask: Gappu has never left his nest! Can you tell him what the main physical regions of India are?
teach.praise: Wow! Mountains, plains, plateau, desert and coasts. India is like a giant map of everything!
teach.nudge: You said some regions. What about the high flat land in the south, or the dry sandy west?

topics.title: The Himalayas and the Northern Plains

learn.hook: 'Himalaya' means 'abode of snow' in Sanskrit. These young, rising mountains feed some of India's mightiest rivers.
points: The Himalayas are young fold mountains. They stretch in an arc along India's northern border.
They have three main parallel ranges: the Greater Himalayas (Himadri, the highest), the Middle Himalayas (Himachal) and the Shiwaliks (the lowest, outer range).
Kangchenjunga, on the border of Sikkim and Nepal, is one of the highest peaks in the world. Mount Everest, the world's highest peak, lies in Nepal.
Snow and glaciers of the Himalayas feed rivers like the Ganga, the Yamuna and the Brahmaputra, which flow all year round.
The Northern Plains lie south of the Himalayas. They were formed by soil laid down by the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra river systems, and are among the most fertile lands on Earth.

example.q: Why do the Ganga and Yamuna keep flowing even in the hot, dry month of May?
steps: They start from glaciers high in the Himalayas (Gangotri and Yamunotri).
In summer, heat melts snow and ice on the mountains.
This meltwater keeps feeding the rivers even when there is no rain.
example.answer: Because they are fed by melting Himalayan snow and glaciers, they are perennial (year-round) rivers.

learn.reallife: Hill towns like Shimla, Mussoorie and Darjeeling are in the Himalayas; families visit them to escape summer heat.

quiz.q: What does the word 'Himalaya' mean?
quiz.explain: In Sanskrit, 'hima' means snow and 'alaya' means home or abode.
quiz.mistake: Guesses the meaning without knowing the Sanskrit roots

quiz.q: Kangchenjunga, one of the world's highest peaks, lies on the border of Sikkim and which country?
quiz.explain: Kangchenjunga stands on the border between Sikkim (India) and Nepal, in the Greater Himalayas.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the countries that border Sikkim

quiz.q: Which is the outermost and lowest range of the Himalayas?
quiz.explain: The Shiwaliks are the southernmost, lowest range, next to the plains.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the order of the three ranges

quiz.q: The Himalayas are called 'young fold mountains' because:
options: They are only a few hundred years old
They were formed recently in Earth's history and are still rising
quiz.explain: In Earth's long history, the Himalayas formed fairly recently by the folding of rock layers, and they are still slowly rising.
quiz.mistake: Takes 'young' to mean young in human years

quiz.q: Why do Himalayan rivers flow throughout the year?
options: They are fed by melting snow and glaciers
It rains every day in the Himalayas
They are fed by the sea
quiz.explain: Snow and glacier melt keeps them flowing even in dry months, so they are perennial.
quiz.mistake: Thinks rivers depend only on rainfall

quiz.q: How were the Northern Plains formed?
options: By soil deposited by rivers over a very long time
By wind blowing sand from the desert
By people filling land with soil
quiz.explain: The Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra and their tributaries carried silt down from the mountains and spread it over the plains.
quiz.mistake: Confuses river-made plains with volcanic or desert land

quiz.q: Which river system flows through Assam in the north-east?
quiz.explain: The Brahmaputra flows through Assam, forming a broad valley.
quiz.mistake: Picks a river of peninsular India

quiz.q: Majuli, one of the world's largest river islands, is found in which river?
quiz.explain: Majuli is a large river island in the Brahmaputra in Assam.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the islands of the Brahmaputra

teach.ask: Gappu wants to fly to the Himalayas. Tell him what they are and why they matter to the plains below.
teach.praise: So the snowy mountains feed the rivers, and the rivers make the plains fertile. Everything is connected!
teach.nudge: Good start! But how do the Himalayas help the farmers in the plains?

learn.hook: The southern half of India is a giant triangle of old rock with hills on both sides and the sea all around.
points: The Peninsular Plateau is a large triangle-shaped tableland made of very old, hard rocks. The Deccan Plateau is its main part.
The Western Ghats (Sahyadri) run along the west edge of the plateau. They are high and continuous, with thick forests and great variety of plants and animals.
The Eastern Ghats run along the east edge. They are lower and broken by rivers like the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri, which flow east into the Bay of Bengal.
Coastal plains lie between the Ghats and the sea: a narrow western coast along the Arabian Sea and a wider eastern coast along the Bay of Bengal with big river deltas.
India's islands: Lakshadweep (coral islands in the Arabian Sea) and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands (in the Bay of Bengal). Barren Island in the Andamans has India's only active volcano.

example.q: Why do most big rivers of the Deccan, like the Godavari and Krishna, flow east into the Bay of Bengal?
steps: The Western Ghats are high, so the western side of the plateau is raised.
The plateau slopes gently down towards the east.
Water flows downhill, so the rivers travel east and form deltas on the east coast.
example.answer: Because the Deccan Plateau slopes from west to east.

learn.reallife: Kerala's backwaters and Goa's beaches are on the western coastal plain; the Sundarbans mangroves are on the delta of the Ganga and Brahmaputra.

quiz.q: Which mountain range is also called the Sahyadri?
quiz.explain: The Western Ghats along the west coast are also known as the Sahyadri.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the Western and Eastern Ghats

quiz.q: How are the Eastern Ghats different from the Western Ghats?
options: They are lower and broken up by rivers
They are in the Thar Desert
quiz.explain: The Eastern Ghats are lower and are cut through by big rivers flowing to the Bay of Bengal.
quiz.mistake: Reverses the features of the two Ghats

quiz.q: Which river of the plateau flows into the Bay of Bengal?
quiz.explain: The Godavari flows east to the Bay of Bengal. The Narmada and Tapi flow west into the Arabian Sea.
quiz.mistake: Does not know which rivers flow west

quiz.q: Lakshadweep islands are made mainly of:
quiz.explain: Lakshadweep's islands are coral islands built over a long time by tiny sea creatures.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Lakshadweep with volcanic Barren Island

quiz.q: Where is India's only active volcano?
options: Barren Island in the Andaman Sea
quiz.explain: Barren Island, part of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, has India's only active volcano.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any high mountain is a volcano

quiz.q: Which coastal plain of India is wider and has large river deltas?
quiz.explain: The east coast is wider because big rivers deposit soil there and form deltas.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the western coast is wider

quiz.q: The Sundarbans, famous for mangroves and the Royal Bengal tiger, lie in the delta of:
quiz.explain: The Sundarbans are on the vast delta formed where the Ganga and Brahmaputra meet the Bay of Bengal.
quiz.mistake: Does not link the Sundarbans to Bengal's rivers

quiz.q: Why are the rocks of the Peninsular Plateau special?
options: They are made of sand only
They are among the oldest rocks in India
quiz.explain: The plateau is built of ancient hard rocks, much older than the Himalayas.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the plateau is younger than the Himalayas

teach.ask: Gappu is confused: what is a plateau, and what lies around India's plateau?
teach.praise: A big rocky table with Ghats on its sides and coasts all around. I can picture it!
teach.nudge: Nice! But what hills stand on the west and east edges of the plateau?
